Class WarDiplomacyEngine

java.lang.Object
org.ether.society.core.engine.AbstractSimulationEngine
org.ether.society.engines.tier2.theories.WarDiplomacyEngine
All Implemented Interfaces:
SimulationEngineModule
public class WarDiplomacyEngine extends AbstractSimulationEngine
Geopolitical Conflict invalid input: '&' Border War Engine. Models: 1. War declarations based on expansionism (Asabiyyah), resource scarcity, target instability, and boundary friction (sigma_friction). 2. Military battles using the youth adult recruitment cohort (pop15to24) with boundary friction resistance. 3. Dynamic territorial conquest and border shifting.
Version:
1.0.0-beta.3
Author:
Silvere Martin-Michiellot

    • calculateBoundaryFriction

      public static double calculateBoundaryFriction(H3Cell c1, H3Cell c2)
      Calculates the boundary friction (sigma_friction) between two adjacent cells. Incorporates sovereignty gradient mismatch, terrain movement friction, and elevation declivity.

    • processGeopoliticalConflicts

      public static void processGeopoliticalConflicts(List<Polity> nations, List<H3Cell> cells)

      Parameters:
      nations - list of active polities
      cells - list of all grid cells

    • processGeopoliticalConflicts

      public static void processGeopoliticalConflicts(List<Polity> nations, List<H3Cell> cells, Scenario scenario)
      Executes geopolitical conflict pass across active nations. Evaluates territorial adjacency, war desire, and resolves border skirmishes.

    • getAverageBorderFriction

      public static double getAverageBorderFriction(Polity n1, Polity n2)
      Backward-compatible helper method to compute average boundary friction between two polities. Returns -1 if nations do not share a border within the projection distance (150 km).

    • getBorderContact

      public static WarDiplomacyEngine.BorderContact getBorderContact(Polity n1, Polity n2, WarDiplomacyEngine.BoundingBox b1, WarDiplomacyEngine.BoundingBox b2)
      Computes boundary contact and average friction across common border cells of two nations. Uses spatial hash binning and fast equirectangular rejection in O(N1).
